report.summary: Chunk 3 of 4: contains graph_brief function and helper _emit, with neighbourhood walk loop and layer rendering logic; claims about budget reservation and rendering order are checkable.
risks: graph_brief | medium | The index is caught as Exception (BLE001), which may hide genuine errors; but docstring says 'Never raises for a missing or unreadable index'. | Confirm if any non-IndexError exceptions should be re-raised.

_emit | medium | 'spent' is incremented per line but not reset if budget exceeded; header cost is added after checking lines, potentially allowing overshoot by header length. | Verify that header cost is correctly accounted before or after line checks.
_neighbourhood | low | The function iterates up to 'hops' but uses max(0, hops) which may differ from caller's expectation if hops is negative. | Confirm that negative hops is handled as zero.
graph_brief | low | 'rels' is built from targets with deduplication but using dict.fromkeys; order is preserved only in Python 3.7+. | Ensure Python version compatibility or use OrderedDict.

claims.text: Never raises for a missing or unreadable index: a lane that cannot get a brief must still be able to run with none. A brief is context, not a gate.
claims.why: The code uses try/except Exception and sets index = {} on failure, so no exception propagates.

claims.text: The header is written last but must not escape the budget, so its space is reserved up front. A brief that overshoots by exactly the size of its own preamble is the kind of off-by-a-section that only shows up as a truncated prompt at the far end.
claims.why: The value of _HEADER_RESERVE is not defined in this chunk; the claim that space is reserved up front is partially checkable (spent is initialized to _HEADER_RESERVE) but the correctness depends on the constant's value.

claims.text: Priority matters because the layers are wildly different sizes: the 1-hop symbol layer around ``offload.py`` alone is 495 lines, and emitting it first consumed the entire budget and dropped the import layer -- the smallest and most valuable of the three, and the only one that answers "what will I break". Small high-value layers are rendered first and DISPLAYED in reading order.
claims.why: The code calls _emit first for imports (small/high-value) then for symbols (larger), so rendering order is priority-order. Display order is not enforced here but is implied by the order of rendered dict entries; the claim about display order is uncheckable (depends on caller).

claims.text: Artefact importers are filtered HERE as well as in the neighbourhood. Measured: the first brief for ``shift.py`` had no artefact neighbour left and still printed "<- imported by runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py", because a reverse edge is read straight off the index and never passed through the walk.
claims.why: The code explicitly filters inc with `if not _is_artefact(s)`, so artefacts are excluded. The comment explains why this filter is needed.

observations.what: The _neighbourhood function uses `max(0, hops)` which may treat negative hops as zero, but the docstring does not specify behavior for negative hops.

The variable `spent` is incremented per line, but the header cost is added after checking lines; if a line fits but adding the header would exceed budget, the header is added anyway, potentially causing overshoot.
The index is loaded via `cached_index(root)` which may return a stale index if the filesystem has changed; no invalidation logic is visible.
The function `_deep_only_modules` is called but not defined in this chunk; its behavior is unknown.
The function `_tail_matches` is called but not defined in this chunk; its behavior is unknown.
The constant `DEEP_EDGE_MARK` is used but not defined in this chunk.
